ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory risk-based AML/CFT screening of partners, UBOs, and authorized representatives. The protocol must cover Luxembourg Financial Intelligence Unit (CRF) guidance, EU consolidated financial sanctions list, UN Security Council sanctions, OFAC SDN list, and domestic PEP databases; enhanced due diligence is required where any UBO is a PEP, resides in a high-risk jurisdiction, or holds a council-controlled token issuance model.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: Luxembourg Business Registers (LBR), online portal at https://www.lbr.lu (formerly Registre de Commerce et des Sociétés)
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: Names must be entered in the RCS/LBR using Latin-script characters. Non-Latin script names require a French or German transliteration. The name must be distinctive, not misleading, and must contain or be accompanied by the legal form indicator 'SCSp' or the equivalent 'Special Limited Partnership'.
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: Within 30 days of rejection, the applicant may submit a revised name reservation through the LBR portal. If the rejection is maintained, the applicant may file a written appeal with the Registrar of the Luxembourg Business Registers, accompanied by legal arguments and supporting documents; a further appeal may be brought before the Luxembourg District Court (Tribunal d'arrondissement) in commercial matters within two months of receipt of the refusal.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: A virtual office for administrative correspondence may be permitted, but the SCSp must maintain a duly registered Luxembourg registered office and ensure that central management and substance (tax residency) requirements are demonstrably met; a purely virtual seat without any substance is not advisable for the AI/LLM API token-generation business model.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: Low to medium: approximately 25% for a substance-light offshore-looking SCSp; below 10% where the partnership maintains physical substance, local bank accounts, and local decision-making records.

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Law of 10 August 1915 on Commercial Companies, as amended, Articles 905-1 et seq. (SCSp regime introduced by Law of 12 July 2013); Civil Code, Book III, Title X.
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Luxembourg Business Registers (LBR) – Registre de Commerce et des Sociétés (RCS)
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Deed of Formation (Contrat de Société or Authentic Notarial Deed) filed via RCS e-file and published in the Recueil Électronique des Sociétés (RES)
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: None. The SCSp has no statutory minimum capital. Contributions are freely determined in the partnership agreement. No escrow account is required for cash contributions.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: RESOLVED: (1) that the initial subscription list for the partnership interests in the SCSp be approved and accepted; (2) that the registered office be established at the address stated in the partnership agreement and that the General Partner conclude any lease and utility contracts required; (3) that [name of manager] be appointed as manager, with authority to represent the partnership, operate bank accounts, and enter into AI/API platform agreements; (4) that all jurisdictional filings for RCS registration, VAT registration, and the general data protection register be made forthwith; and (5) that each officer be indemnified against lawful expenses incurred by reason of office.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Prepare and execute the SCSp partnership agreement
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Parties or, if an authentic deed is elected, a Luxembourg civil-law notary
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Draft the deed of formation covering firm name, SCSp status, registered office in Luxembourg, corporate purpose dedicated to generative AI and LLM API inference services, contribution schedule, profit distribution ratios, and management powers of the General Partner. Execute the agreement, with signature pages reflecting all General and Limited Partners. Notarise only if real property or other assets requiring public filing are contributed.
required_dossiers: Executed partnership agreement
Passport/ID copies of General Partner and Limited Partners
Proof of Luxembourg registered office address
Draft contribution schedule and subscription list
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the deed is queried for incomplete mandatory content (name, purpose, capital, office), amend it by a supplementary private deed and sign again before re-filing.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: File and register the SCSp with the Luxembourg Business Registers
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Luxembourg Business Registers – RCS (online portal: lbr.lu)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Create a My LBR account; complete the company registration questionnaire; submit the executed deed, legal data forms, and UBO preliminary data. Pay the publication fee for the Recueil Electronique des Sociétés and the RCS filing fee. Upon validation, receive the RCS number and publication extract in the RES.
required_dossiers: Executed partnership agreement or notarial deed
RCS Form A (identification data of legal entity)
RCS Form B (managers/General Partner details)
Consent of the General Partner and manager
Proof of registered office (lease or ownership document)
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If LBR issues a request for regularization, resubmit the missing document or amended form within 15 calendar days; otherwise the application is rejected and a fresh filing is required.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Confirm establishment licence position for AI software services
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Ministry of the Economy – Guichet.lu (Autorisation d'établissement)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Establish whether the AI LLM API platform is an non-regulated intellectual service. For ISIC 6201 software publishing and data processing, no professional establishment permit is ordinarily required under the Law of 2 September 2011. Submit a feasibility question to Guichet.lu within 15 days after RCS registration to obtain administrative confirmation if uncertainty remains.
required_dossiers: RCS registration extract
Partnership agreement excerpt
Descriptive business plan of the AI/LLM API services
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the Ministry classifies the activity as regulated, apply for an establishment permit through Guichet.lu and produce manager qualifications or relevant professional indemnity cover within the statutory deadline.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Register with tax, social security, and statistical authorities
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Administration de l'Enregistrement, des Domaines et de la TVA (AEDT); Administration des Contributions Directes; Centre Commun de la Sécurité Sociale (CCSS); STATEC
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Use MyGuichet or the AEDT Enterprise Register portal to request VAT registration. For a fiscally transparent SCSp, no corporate income tax is levied at entity level, but annual tax filings are still required. Register with CCSS if employees are to be hired, and complete the social security entry formalities within 8 days of first engagement.
required_dossiers: RCS registration extract
Partnership agreement
Identification of beneficial owners
Bank account details (template)
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If registration is delayed, file a voluntary tax registration request with AEDT and remit any late VAT exposure with interest; spontaneous disclosure ordinarily reduces penalties.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Complete UBO declaration, data protection register, and payment-rails compliance
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Luxembourg Business Registers (RBE, ultimate beneficial owner register); Commission Nationale pour la Protection des Données (CNPD); Commission de Surveillance du Secteur Financier (CSSF)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Lodge UBO identification with RBE within one month of registration. Register as a data processor or controller with the CNPD if the platform processes personal data in the course of LLM inference. If the API platform accepts USDC stablecoins, assess whether third-party payment processors can be used without triggering a CSSF VASP licence; otherwise apply for VASP authorisation.
required_dossiers: UBO identification forms and supporting ID documents
CNPD data-processing register form
AML/CFT policy if payment services are processed directly
Third-party payment processor agreement (Stripe/USDC wirefall)
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: For UBO omissions, file corrected data promptly and pay administrative penalties if assessed. For VASP doubts, submit a CSSF interpretive request or obtain legal opinion before handling any digital asset in a manner that constitutes a regulated virtual asset service.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Ministry of the Economy – Directorate General for Industry (reference for exemptions; no industrial operating licence applies to ISIC 6201 AI software services)
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: Not applicable – statutory exemption: no sectoral manufacturing or occupational licence required for generative AI and LLM API platform activities; only data-centre hosting and ordinary office permits may be relevant.

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Not required – the activity is a non-industrial software service; only electronic/electrical equipment handling is subject to WEEE registration if the operator imports or places servers, workstations, or related hardware on the Luxembourg market.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: No process wastewater or VOC emission thresholds are applicable. For any physical infrastructure, comply with EU Directive 2012/19/EU on WEEE, Directive 2011/65/EU on RoHS, and Regulation (EU) 2019/1021 on persistent organic pollutants. General municipal wastewater discharge limits for office and data-centre facilities apply under local water regulations.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: For a leased office/data-centre suite, obtain the fire-safety certification under the Luxembourg Fire Safety Code, verify electrical installation conformity and structural load certificates, and comply with Article L.411-10 of the Labour Code for occupant health and safety. If the gateway is purely virtual with no physical office, a registered agent address suffices and no site-specific occupational clearance is required.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Administration des contributions directes (ACD) for direct taxes; Administration de l'enregistrement, des domaines et de la TVA (AEDT) for VAT; consolidated electronic filing portal: MyGuichet.lu (https://myguichet.lu).
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: The SCSp, being an unincorporated special limited partnership, is fiscally transparent for Luxembourg income tax purposes but must register for VAT when making Luxembourg-taxable supplies. A non-established operator must file the VAT registration application with the AEDT via MyGuichet.lu prior to the first taxable activity. Required package: partnership agreement (contrat de société), RCS extract (where the SCSp is registered), identity documents of the general partner, and proof of business establishment. The AEDT then issues a Luxembourg VAT identification number (format LU followed by 8 alphanumeric characters); the ACD uses the RCS matricule number for corporate tax records.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: Default fiscal transparency applies to the SCSp; partners are taxed individually in their respective jurisdictions. Under Article 175 LIR, the partnership may elect, subject to statutory conditions, to be taxed as a corporate taxpayer. Luxembourg's anti-hybrid rules (Law of 21 December 2018 transposing ATAD) re-characterize mismatching transparent entities and deny benefits where double non-taxation arises. There is no U.S.-style check-the-box regime; entity classification is governed by domestic LIR principles and OECD partnership report guidance.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: Value Added Tax (TVA - Taxe sur la valeur ajoutée)
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: No registration threshold for non-established taxable persons: the first euro of Luxembourg-taxable supplies triggers VAT registration. Domestic small-business exemption (franchise d'assujettissement) applies up to EUR 35,000 annual turnover for service providers. Intra-EU distance sales of goods and cross-border B2C digital services are subject to the EUR 10,000 Union-wide threshold, above which the OSS/IOSS regimes apply.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: Luxembourg does not currently impose real-time fiscal clearance, API-based tax reporting, digital stamping, or mandatory B2B e-invoicing. Invoices must satisfy Article 75 LGTVA content requirements; OSS/IOSS returns are filed through the EU single portal administered by the AEDT. The EU VAT in the Digital Age (ViDA) package is expected to introduce mandatory e-invoicing and digital transaction reporting for Luxembourg taxable persons by 2030.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Exports of tangible goods to third-country destinations qualify for a 0% VAT rate upon export. For AI/LLM API services (electronically supplied services), place-of-supply rules apply: B2B supplies to non-Luxembourg customers are outside Luxembourg VAT (reverse charge), B2C supplies to non-EU consumers are outside Luxembourg VAT, and B2C supplies to EU consumers are taxable in the consumer's member state via OSS. Zero-rating for services is substantiated by documented customer location, business status, and use-and-enjoyment analysis rather than physical customs clearance.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Executed AI/LLM API service agreement stating customer jurisdiction and service delivery terms
VIES-validated VAT identification number of the B2B customer inside the EU
Business register extract or equivalent corporate proof for non-EU B2B customers
Tax invoice with correct place-of-supply coding and VAT treatment statement
Inward remittance / FX settlement evidence (SWIFT, Stripe, or USDC on-chain records) supporting repatriation
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: The AEDT anti-fraud unit (ULAF) and the ACD audit division may challenge export zero-rating and OSS positions. Unsupported claims trigger VAT reassessment, statutory late interest, and fines; fraudulent schemes expose the entity to criminal penalties (imprisonment up to five years and fines up to EUR 250,000), retrospective clawback of input VAT credits, publication of judgments, and cross-border intelligence sharing through Eurofisc.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Banque centrale du Luxembourg (BCL), acting in conjunction with the Luxembourg Ministry of Finance, the Commission de Surveillance du Secteur Financier (CSSF) for AML/CFT supervision, and the European Central Bank (ECB) for euro monetary policy and BOP statistical reporting.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: Luxembourg is a full EMU member state; the euro is fully and freely convertible for both current account payments (AI subscription fees, API royalties, cloud hosting costs, licensing) and capital account transactions (capital contributions to the SCSp, profit distributions, and liquidation proceeds). No exchange-control restrictions, conversion licenses, or repatriation permits apply. Non-resident partners may remit partnership earnings without BCL approval, subject only to general EU AML/CFT due diligence, tax transparency obligations (e.g., CRS, FATCA, DAC6 where relevant), economic substance expectations, and compliance with EU/UN sanctions. For a tax-transparent SCSp, partnership distributions are not subject to Luxembourg withholding tax, but the bank may require an up-to-date beneficial ownership declaration and proof of the distribution resolution before processing the remittance.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: Luxembourg imposes no export-proceeds surrender requirement, no mandatory conversion ratio, and no holding-period obligation for export receipts. All proceeds from AI LLM API services, denominated in EUR or foreign currency, may be kept on account, reinvested, or transferred abroad without BCL consent. The only ongoing administrative obligations are statistical classification under EU Balance of Payments (BOP) Regulation (EC) No 184/2005 and BCL reporting instructions: receipts for software-enabled API services are classified under the BOP services item 'Telecommunications, computer and information services'. No timeline or conversion percentage is prescribed.

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Feasibility rating: Medium-to-Low for an unregulated overseas EMI, Low for non-EEA digital banks. Luxembourg law permits the use of EEA-licensed Electronic Money Institutions (EMIs) for payment processing, but established tier-1 Luxembourg banks generally reject EMIs as the primary treasury account for a partnership with non-resident partners because the EMI cannot guarantee local beneficiary AML, sanctions, and economic substance oversight. A viable hybrid model is to use a regulated EU EMI (e.g., a CSSF/ECB-licensed EMI) only as a low-value middleware for streaming API customer settlement, while the main SCSp treasury and all capital flows are cleared through a Luxembourg commercial bank. Any cryptocurrency-backed EMI or crypto-currency payment gateway (USDC/crypto) must be isolated from corporate treasury and can be used only for customer invoicing if an EU-located, AML-compliant payment service provider handles conversion to fiat and passes clean funds to the bank account. Full bank KYC of the EMI fallback is mandatory.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: Luxembourg does not impose a statutory physical-presence requirement for bank onboarding, but the CSSF AML/CFT framework and bank policies generally require personal identification and an adequate compliance interview. In practice, the SCSp's manager (or a duly appointed authorised representative with a Luxembourg professional mandate) must be identified through either (i) a physical meeting with a bank officer or a notary, or (ii) a secured video-identification procedure if the bank offers it. For SCSp structures with non-EU partners, most tier-1 banks require at least one face-to-face interview of the general partner or authorised manager, or a completed CSSF-compliant video identification from a notary/public officer in the partner's jurisdiction. Remote opening is possible for fully European/EU-domiciled partners with clean source-of-wealth documentation, but 100% remote opening for an SCSp owning AI SaaS revenues is unlikely due to partnership layer complexity.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Non-resident corporate partners without a regulated manager or local substance
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Updated partnership agreement (contrat de société); notarised certificate of registered office from the Luxembourg notary; RCS excerpt (extrait RCS) proving valid registration of the SCSp; Luxembourg tax authority confirmation of EORI and VAT status; detailed ownership structure chart identifying all ultimate beneficial owners; CRS self-certifications and FATCA forms for each partner; proof of source of funds through bank references, audited financial statements, or certified tax filings; professional reference letters from an EU lawyer/accountant.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Use of cryptocurrency or USDC in the customer payment flow
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Written business model narrative explaining token-token and token-fiat settlement; list of regulated flat-on-ramp partners and blockchain analytics reports (e.g., Chainalysis or Elliptic) showing the absence of high-risk wallet exposure; a group AML policy compliant with AMLD5/AMLD6; customer onboarding and identity verification procedures for API subscribers; detailed invoices for all commercial transactions; confirmation that no crypto-to-crypto transfers occur from treasury accounts.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: High transaction velocity relative to declared substance and partnership equity
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Substantiated 24-month business plan and financial projections; explanation of the SCSp's operating role and revenue model; evidence of Luxembourg economic substance such as local office lease, local manager or service provider contract, local bank account, and board of partners minutes; sample customer contracts with AI API usage terms; work-flow diagrams connecting the SCSp, the monetised IP, and the API platform; bank reference letters and tax clearance certificates from relevant jurisdictions.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Opaque beneficial ownership or offshore tax haven exposure
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: A signed declaration confirming the SCSp's place of effective management and tax-filing position; beneficial ownership register (Registre des bénéficiaires effectifs) confirmation or, if the SCSp has no natural-person beneficial owner, a legal memorandum with a negative declaration; validity proof of all corporate partners; residency certificates and public economic substance evidence for each partner; a copy of the audit mandate if the partnership is voluntarily audited; regulatory and reputational-due-diligence reports on partners.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Inbound non-resident capital contributions must be wired to the SCSp's operational or escrow account using the SWIFT MT103 format. The payment must clearly reference the partnership legal name, the SCSp's RCS registration number, the injection resolution or subscription agreement, and the BOP direct-investment purpose code. For equity contributions, the ECB/BOP code is F.432 (direct investment – equity capital); for loans from partners, F.431 (direct investment – other capital) must be used. Correspondent clearing should run through TARGET2 for EUR wires or via the SWIFT network for USD/EUR SWIFT MT103 messages. Intermediary banks must be provided with the recipient bank's BIC, the SCSp's IBAN, and the beneficiary account label. The bank may require the partners' source-of-funds evidence, CRS/FATCA certifications, an executed capital contribution deed, and confirmation that the SCSp is not subject to EU sanctions or restrictive measures before crediting the account.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Outbound trade settlements and operational payments from the SCSp should be routed as follows: (i) EUR disbursements to EU counterparties via TARGET2/SEPA with a SEPA Credit Transfer or, for large-value, a SWIFT MT103 with TARGET2 clearing; (ii) non-EUR payments via SWIFT MT103 with the correspondent bank's dedicated currency clearing; (iii) trade-related commitments or infrastructure hardware purchases using a commercial letter of credit (SWIFT MT700/MT707 issued under UCP 600) or a standby LC / bank payment undertaking for deferred obligations; (iv) recurring AI cloud costs and contractor payments via MT103 or SEPA direct debit with invoice scanning for BCL BOP reporting. All outbound instructions must include the underlying purpose code, e.g., services (code 1000/1001), maintenance, or licensing, and sufficient evidence of the invoice to satisfy CSSF AML expectations and BOP statistical filing.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Deliverable FX Forward with an authorised EU credit institution, limited to genuine commercial exposure in USD, EUR, GBP, CHF or JPY
Non-deliverable forward (NDF) for restricted or non-convertible currency exposures where physical delivery is impossible, subject to BCL counterparty eligibility
FX Swap (cash swap and rollover) for short-term liquidity and treasury conversion between EUR and customer settlement currencies
Currency call/put options for protecting minimum revenue conversion rates when the SCSp has a demonstrated AI API revenue stream in USD
Cross-currency interest rate swap (CCIRS) primarily used to align a minor commercial loan or partner capital note into a stable fixed-rate EUR profile
Plain-vanilla FX/deposit-based corridor swaps with a Luxembourg-authorized counterparty, expressly prohibited for speculative or non-underlying positions

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual accounts deposit (dépôt des comptes annuels) at the RCS, only when the SCSp has legal personality or is expressly required by its partnership agreement
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Luxembourg Business Registers – Registre de Commerce et des Sociétés (RCS)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within six months after the financial year-end; if the financial year is the calendar year, no later than 30 June
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: RCS will issue a reminder; continued failure exposes the general partner to administrative fines up to EUR 1,000 and potential judicial dissolution or strike-off proceedings initiated by the Public Prosecutor.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Luxembourg Business Registers – Registre des Bénéficiaires Effectifs (RBE)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Initial filing within one month of RCS registration; annual confirmation no later than 12 months after the last declaration; any change in direct or indirect ownership exceeding 25% must be filed within one month
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Sustained non-filing attracts criminal fines up to EUR 1,250 and/or imprisonment against responsible officers; the RBE may also block the entity from obtaining official extracts until compliance is restored.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual RCS data update and confirmation of registered particulars (registered office, general partner, managers, and statutory object)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Luxembourg Business Registers – Trade and Companies Register (RCS)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within one month of any change to registered facts; annual confirmation recommended on each anniversary of initial registration
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Failure to update registered particulars exposes the SCSp to RCS corrective proceedings, administrative fines up to EUR 500, and inability to obtain certificates of good standing.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual statutory register audit and certification of completeness (register of partners, general partner decisions, and capital contributions)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Registered office of the SCSp; records inspectable by Luxembourg RCS, RBE, AML/CSF authorities, and notaries on demand
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: At each financial year-end, before the RBE annual confirmation is submitted
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Incomplete statutory records are treated as non-maintained books and may result in AML/CSF administrative fines, adverse findings in regulatory due diligence, or criminal sanctions for falsification in cases of deliberate alteration.

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: Mandatory independent audit applies if the SCSp is a regulated investment fund, a public-interest entity, or, if it has legal personality, exceeds two of the following three thresholds: balance sheet total EUR 4,400,000; net turnover EUR 8,800,000; average workforce 25 employees. Exempt SCSp may nevertheless undergo a voluntary certified audit for investor protection.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: Luxembourg GAAP under the amended Law of 10 August 1915 on commercial companies; IFRS may be adopted for consolidated financial statements or investor reporting where the partnership agreement so provides.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: The SCSp must identify every indirect or direct beneficial owner with more than 25% of the partnership interest, voting rights, or economic entitlement. Any partnership interest transfer that changes the UBO must be filed within one month. A re-confirmation of the existing RBE data must occur at least every 12 months from the last declaration.
mandatory_on_site_statutory_registers: Register of Limited Partners and Capital Contributions
General Partner Management Register and Powers of Attorney
Minute Book of Partner Resolutions and Written Consents

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: USD 5,000 – USD 15,000 per year if audited; USD 0 for exempt SCSp

corporate_income_tax_regime.statutory_headline_rate: 24.94% (combined CIT 18.19% inclusive of unemployment surcharge plus municipal business tax at 6.75% in Luxembourg City)
corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: Luxembourg does not apply a general tax holiday; available incentives include: (i) 80% exemption for qualifying net IP income under the IP regime (effective rate circa 5%), (ii) full tax transparency of an SCSp with profits taxed at partner level, and (iii) financing and liquidity? Actually, SCSp transparency is the key effective relief: no CIT/MBT at entity level.
